specs.title: BSS-0001: Blockspace Standards Specification process
specs.abstract:
This document defines how Blockspace Standards Specifications (BSS) are proposed, numbered,
reviewed, tested and advanced. It fixes the status lifecycle, the required sections of every
specification, the rules for test vectors, and the role of the editors.

specs.title: BSS-0002: Blockspace attribution (the Meter)
specs.abstract:
The block.space Meter assigns ("attributes") the bytes of the Bitcoin chain to protocols and
tokens, and reports them in three **books** (A, B, C) and two **denominations** (`bytes`,
`vbytes`). This document fixes the vocabulary, the identifiers and the response shapes that
consumers of the Meter API rely on. It also records, as open questions, every attribution rule
that the available sources do not define. It does not specify an attribution algorithm: none is
written down anywhere the editors could find.

specs.title: BSS-0003: Collection certification attestation
specs.abstract:
A collection attestation is a signed JSON statement. It says which inscriptions belong to a
collection as of a block height, and gives statistics over them that anyone can recompute with
their own ord server. Membership comes from on-chain evidence only: children of the collection's
parent inscription, and a membership manifest that is itself inscribed as a child of that parent.
The attestation is serialised with a canonical JSON profile of RFC 8785 and hashed with the BIP340
tagged hash `block.space/collection-attestation/v1`. The digest is signed with BIP340 Schnorr.
This document specifies the JSON structure, the canonicalisation, the digest, the signature, key
publication, the membership methods and the verification procedure.

specs.title: BSS-0004: Parent-linked collection standard (Degent collection profile)
specs.abstract:
This document specifies how items of an Ordinals collection are minted so that membership is
provable on chain. Every new item is inscribed with a parent tag that names the collection's
parent inscription. The reveal transaction spends the parent UTXO and returns it to the
collection, so ord records the parent/child link. The document fixes the envelope bytes, the
parent-tag encoding, the commit output, the reveal layout and the sat-placement rule, and the
checks the collection's parent signer makes. For the degent.club profile it also fixes three
product tiers by content bytes, two transport lanes by exact transaction weight, and the per-block
weight budget of the block lane. Items minted before parent links existed join the collection
through an inscribed membership manifest (BSS-0003 §3).

specs.title: BSS-0005: Reveal PSBT profiles (half-signed 0x81, wallet-signed, rescue)
specs.abstract:
A parent-linked inscription (BSS-0004) needs two signatures that come from two parties at
different times. The minter signs the commit input when it orders. The collection's parent signer
signs the parent input later. This document specifies the PSBTs that carry the minter's half of the
reveal, in two models:

- **K_e model (half-signed)**: the browser signs the commit input with an ephemeral key K_e and
  `SIGHASH_ALL|SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY` (**0x81**). The signature fixes every output, and the parent
  input can still be attached. The legacy `SIGHASH_SINGLE|SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY` (**0x83**) profile
  is described for compatibility and is deprecated. Rescue is a fresh transaction re-signed with
  K_e.
- **Wallet-signed model**: the leaf key is a key the user's wallet controls, the internal key is
  NUMS, and the wallet signs an ordinary tapscript PSBT with a sighash its software accepts.

The document fixes the transaction template, the PSBT fields (also in machine-readable form in
`profiles/bss-0005-psbt-profile.json`), the verification a service performs before storing a
reveal, and the rescue paths.

specs.title: BSS-0006: Sign in with Bitcoin (SIWB) message format
specs.abstract:
Sign in with Bitcoin (SIWB) adapts EIP-4361 ("Sign-In with Ethereum") to Bitcoin wallets. A server
issues a challenge message that binds a domain, an address, a network, a single-use nonce and a
validity window. The wallet signs the message with a BIP-322 *simple* signature (P2TR key path or
P2WPKH), or with a legacy `signmessage` signature (P2PKH, P2WPKH, P2SH-P2WPKH). The server
verifies the fields in a fixed order and consumes the nonce last. This document fixes the exact
message text, the field syntax, the canonical-form rule and the verification order that
`@bsh/identity` implements.

specs.title: BSS-0007: Component manifest and estate catalog
specs.abstract:
Every package, service and app in a Blockspace repository declares itself in a
`component.yaml`: its name, owner, kind, lifecycle, allowed dependencies, the contracts it
provides and consumes, its stores and its secret *paths*. A generator compiles the manifests of a
repository into a committed `catalog/catalog.json`. Repositories vendored into each other (git
submodules) appear there as *external* components with their origin, which joins the catalogs of
the estate. This document specifies the manifest (`schemas/component.schema.json`, vendored
byte-identical from the reference), the catalog (`schemas/catalog.schema.json`), and the
validation rules.
